name: Millbrook United

location.about: A big Midlands city of about 900,000, grown up along the Mill Brook where a hundred water wheels once turned the brass and button works. The brass trade made it rich, the car plants kept it busy, and the club is the biggest thing in the city - and, for a few seasons now, one of the richest in the land.

colours.story: Old gold and black - the brass of the city's foundries and the soot that came with it. The colours were picked in 1879 by the founders, workers at Hadley's Brass Mill, and have never changed.

home.shirt: old gold with a black collar and black cuffs

third.shirt: white with a thin gold pinstripe

rivals.why: the old enemy across the city boundary - the biggest crowd of the season, every season, since 1883
the last day of 1990-91, when Bramhall won the title at Millstream Park - the city has never forgiven them

history.title: The brass mill boys
history.text: Founded in 1879 by workers at Hadley's Brass Mill. The Founders' Cup came in 1899, and second place in the League in 1910. The club moved to Millstream Park, on the old mill pond, in 1904.

history.title: The first golden age
history.text: Champions in 1920, second three times in five seasons in the twenties (1923, 1924, 1928), Founders' Cup winners in 1931 and 1933, and champions again in 1938.

history.title: Highs and a fall
history.text: The Founders' Cup in 1947 and the title in 1949, the cup again in 1954. Then the slow decline: relegated in 1965 for the only time, and back up as runners-up in 1968.

history.title: Ron Pickering's Golds
history.text: The Charter Cup in 1974, second in 1978, then Ron Pickering's great side: the Double in 1985, the Founders' Cup in 1987 and another Double in 1989. On the last day of 1990-91 they needed a draw at home to Bramhall to win the title - and lost.

history.title: Cups and near misses
history.text: A team built for the cups: the Charter Cup in 1993, 1996, 1999 and 2005, the Founders' Cup in 1994 and 1995 - but only second place in the league in 1998 and 2017.

history.title: New money
history.text: An American investment group bought the club in 2021 and spent: a new North Stand, a squad to match Northwick's - and the Founders' Cup and Charter Cup in 2024 and the Charter Cup again in 2025. The title is the one thing missing.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1920 = 1919-20).

legends.name: Ron Pickering
legends.note: Two Doubles (1985 and 1989) and four other cups. The Pickering Stand is named after him.

legends.name: Walter Hadley
legends.note: Owner of the brass mill whose workers started the club.

legends.name: Callum Barnes
legends.note: The star of the 2024 and 2025 cup wins.

records.attendance: 78,412 v Stonecross Albion, Founders' Cup fifth round, 1938 (old Millstream Park)

badge.about: The water wheel for the Mill Brook and the mills that made the city; the brook beneath it; the old gold and black of the brass works. Motto 'Semper Volvens' - always turning.
badge.design: A black heraldic shield with a thin old-gold border. In the centre, a large old-gold water wheel with spokes and paddles. Beneath it, three wavy old-gold lines for the brook. 'MILLBROOK UNITED' arched above the shield in old-gold capitals, and an old-gold ribbon beneath reading 'SEMPER VOLVENS' in black, with '1879' on the ribbon's ends.

ground.name: Millstream Park

stands.name: Pickering Stand
stands.features: the main stand: dressing rooms, tunnel and dugouts on the halfway line, boxes between the tiers; Ron Pickering's statue outside

stands.name: Brook End
stands.features: the home end - two steep tiers in gold seats; the old mill pond, now an ornamental lake with a restored water wheel, right behind it

stands.name: North Stand
stands.features: the new owners' stand: three tiers, glass-fronted hospitality, the club's museum; away fans in the lower tier corner

stands.name: East Stand
stands.features: an older two-tier stand with a long, low roof - the next one to be rebuilt

ground.corners: the southern corners filled in (1990s); the northern corners part of the new North Stand
ground.roof: four roofs - the North Stand's new sweeping one, the others older cantilevers
ground.surroundings: the old mill pond and its restored water wheel behind the Brook End, the Mill Brook running past, red-brick factories turned into flats, the city's towers on the skyline
ground.atmosphere: big, loud and expectant - the Brook End sings, and the city expects trophies now
